controversies.title: Explicit instruction advantage versus spontaneous/implicit ability
competing_positions: Explicit instruction often improves studied target outcomes and can accelerate learning.
Controlled/explicitly accessible test gains do not establish spontaneous or implicit ability.
controversies.current_resolution: Use explicit information when it solves a documented processing/knowledge problem, but require target-skill independent evidence before claiming usable ability.
controversies.would_change_if: Direct target-population evidence showed that explicit support reliably harms or uniquely improves delayed spontaneous performance under Nếp-like conditions.

controversies.title: Prompts versus recasts / supplied correction
competing_positions: Prompts can produce stronger outcomes by requiring learner-generated repair.
Recasts/supplied models can be more useful when the learner lacks enough knowledge to self-repair.
controversies.current_resolution: No universal winner; choose feedback by repair readiness and error consequence, preserving the pre-feedback attempt.
controversies.would_change_if: Near-A0 comparative data identified a stable feedback policy that dominates across delayed changed-context outcomes without excessive cognitive or interaction cost.

controversies.title: Lexical coverage threshold versus continuous comprehension relationship
competing_positions: 95–98% coverage values are useful practical regions for relatively independent comprehension in some modalities.
Comprehension generally changes continuously with coverage and modality/task/learner conditions prevent one universal threshold.
controversies.current_resolution: Use coverage as a learner-material compatibility signal, never as a universal mastery/unlock threshold.
controversies.would_change_if: Large replicated target-population studies established robust modality-specific decision thresholds with low false-ready/false-locked rates.
